year_launched.note: ONCC's own pages do not state the exact first OCN administration year on the fetched pages. OCN is widely described as ONCC's foundational/longest-running credential and ONCC was incorporated in 1984, but no verbatim launch year was confirmed from a primary source, so left null rather than guessed.

eligibility.value: All criteria must be met at time of application and examination: (1) a current, active, unencumbered RN license in the US, its territories, or Canada; (2) a minimum of 2,000 hours of adult oncology nursing practice within the four years (48 months) prior to application (practice may be clinical, administration, education, research, or consultation); (3) a minimum of two years (24 months) of experience as an RN within the four years prior to application; and (4) a minimum of 10 contact hours of nursing continuing education in oncology (or an academic elective in oncology nursing) within the three years (36 months) prior to application.

experience_requirement.value: 2,000 hours adult oncology nursing practice in prior 48 months + 24 months RN experience in prior 48 months + 10 oncology CE contact hours in prior 36 months. Unlike some BCEN exams these are hard eligibility gates, not recommendations.

exam_format.value: Computer-based test delivered through PSI (psiexams.com). 165 multiple-choice questions, of which 145 are scored and 20 are unscored pretest items. Time limit 3 hours. Same-day (immediate) test results. Authorization to Test (ATT) opens an almost-immediate 90-day testing window.

question_count_scored.note: ONCC page states 165 questions; the 145-scored / 20-pretest split is reported by corroborating prep sources (TestPrepReview) and is the long-standing ONCC structure, but the split was not stated verbatim on the fetched ONCC page.

passing_score.value: Scaled score of at least 55 (on ONCC's scaled-score system). The cut score is set by a criterion-referenced Passing Score Study using the judgment of panels of oncology nursing professionals; it is not a simple percentage of items correct.
passing_score.note: Scaled minimum of 55 reported by corroborating prep sources and consistent with ONCC's published scaled-score scale; ONCC's task-force page confirms a passing-score study process. Treated as medium confidence.

fee_member.note: ONS (Oncology Nursing Society) / APHON member rate

fee_doubletake.note: Optional DoubleTake add-on (a retake option if the candidate does not pass the first attempt) costs an additional $100 and must be selected/paid when registering for the initial exam.

fee_retake.note: Standard retake fee not stated as a single number on fetched ONCC pages; DoubleTake ($100 add-on) is the published discounted-retake mechanism. Left null rather than guessed.

renewal.value: OCN certification is valid for four years. Most candidates renew via Option 1 (Practice Hours + Professional Development Points) under ONCC's ILNA (Individual Learning Needs Assessment) model: hold current OCN; current active unencumbered RN license; 12 months RN experience within prior 36 months; 1,000 hours of adult oncology nursing practice within prior 30 months; and submit professional-development points matching the subject areas and weighting of the current Test Content Outline. Options 2 (Practice Hours + retest) and 3 (Points + retest) are also available.

renewal_points.note: ONCC's renewal guide states AOCN/AOCNS/CPON learning plans require 50 points; the standard ILNA learning plan for OCN and other RN-level credentials is 100 points, and the renewal guide describes a 100-point plan for nurses who do not take the assessment. Exact per-individual point total is set by each nurse's Test/Assessment Results Report. Treated as medium confidence.

renewal_practice_hours.note: 1,000 hours adult oncology nursing practice within 30 months prior to renewal application (Option 1).

common_confusions.value: OCN (RN-level adult oncology, ONCC) is conflated with BMTCN (ONCC blood & marrow transplant), CBCN (ONCC breast care), CPHON (ONCC pediatric hematology/oncology), AOCNP (ONCC advanced-practice NP credential), and TCTCN (ONCC transplant/cellular therapy). OCN is the foundational adult oncology RN credential; the others are population- or practice-level specific.

salary_context.value: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics OEWS (May 2024) reports a mean annual wage of about $98,430 for registered nurses; oncology and certified specialty nurses frequently earn above the median, and many cancer centers offer certification differentials.

recent_changes.value: ONCC published an updated OCN Test Content Outline (2026 edition, copyright 2025) effective for current testing, built on the 2020/2021 role delineation study of basic adult oncology nursing practice. The six subject areas and their weights are unchanged from the prior 2025 outline. ONCC also convened a 2025 OCN Passing Score Task Force to review the cut score.

blueprint_note: Weights are percentages from the official ONCC 2026 OCN Test Content Outline (copyright ONCC 2025) and sum to 100%. Verified verbatim from the PDF: I. Care Continuum 14%, II. Oncology Nursing Practice 15%, III. Treatment Modalities 20%, IV. Symptom Management and Supportive Care 25%, V. Oncologic Emergencies 16%, VI. Psychosocial Dimensions of Care 10%. These match the Content Outline Data.csv outline exactly.

pass_rate_history.note: ONCC publishes annual Examination Statistics and Pass Rates; the 2024 PDF is image-based and the exact OCN figure could not be machine-extracted. Corroborating sources report an overall OCN pass rate of about 62% (first-time ~65%) in recent years. Treated as medium confidence; verify against ONCC's 2024 Examination Statistics PDF.

discrepancies.detail: src/_data/certs.js lists OCN questions: 165 (canonical project source). ONCC confirms 165 total. Agreement, no conflict. Page uses 165 total with a 145-scored / 20-pretest split.
An early web-search snippet reported Care Continuum 19% / Oncology Nursing Practice 17% / Treatment Modalities 19% / Psychosocial 12%, which conflicts with the official ONCC PDF (14/15/20/10).
discrepancies.resolution: Discarded the search-snippet numbers; used the official 2026 ONCC Test Content Outline PDF, which sums cleanly to 100% and matches the project's CSV outline.

discrepancies.detail: Sources vary: ~62% overall (with ~65% first-time) per most prep sources, vs. a looser 70-80% claim from one secondary source.
discrepancies.resolution: Used ~62% (most-cited, recent) at medium confidence; flagged the 70-80% claim as unreliable.
